title: 4/16/2026 | The City of Bryan, Texas | COM | Letter from the City of Bryan Mayor to the Public Utilities Commission of Texas regarding Large Load Interconnection Rules

documents.text:
=== Mayor City of Bryan PUCT COMMENT LETTER.pdf ===
April 14, 2026



Dear Commissioners,

On behalf of the City of Bryan, I write to emphasize the critical importance of the Commission’s
proposed large load interconnection rules — not only for our community, but for the future of
economic development across Texas and for our nation’s national security and global
competitiveness

At the outset, I wish to highlight three principles that we believe are essential to getting this
framework right.

First, Texas must remain competitive. Communities like Bryan are actively competing for large-
scale industrial and advanced manufacturing projects that require significant, reliable power. These
projects represent long-term investment, job creation, and significant economic growth. If the
regulatory framework becomes overly burdensome or uncertain, those projects will not wait on us
to get it right, they will locate in other states.

Second, flexibility must be preserved -- particularly for communities served by municipal
utilities. Local utilities like Bryan Texas Utilities (BTU) are uniquely positioned to work directly
with customers, align infrastructure with growth, and deliver reliable service in a way that reflects
local conditions. A one-size-fits-all approach risks undermining communities that have
demonstrated the ability to manage growth responsibly.

Third, financial requirements must be structured to enable -- not discourage --investment.
While it is appropriate to require meaningful commitments from large-load customers, excessive
upfront costs or inflexible financial structures risk pricing out legitimate projects. We strongly
support a staged approach to financial commitments, where obligations increase as projects
advance and become more certain, paired with clear and predictable refund mechanisms tied to
energization milestones.

Bryan has a long and proud history of powering growth. Through BTU, beginning with our origin
to meet local needs, we have demonstrated that local leadership, technical expertise, and thoughtful
planning can deliver reliable, affordable power while supporting meaningful economic expansion.
This model has allowed us to compete for and sustain the kinds of projects that strengthen our tax
base and position our region for long-term success.
 Today, Texas stands at an inflection point. The next generation of economic development --
advanced manufacturing, high-tech industry, and large-scale industrial investment -- depends on
our ability to deliver power at scale, with certainty and speed. For Bryan, this is not theoretical.
We are actively engaged in supporting projects that represent significant long-term investment in
our community, including developments requiring substantial load capacity. The City of Bryan
strives to work at the speed of business, not the speed of government.

We fully support the Commission’s commitment to grid reliability and responsible planning.
Those goals are essential. However, it is equally important the regulatory framework reflects the
realities of how large-scale projects are developed and financed. This effort includes ensuring that
cost allocation remains fair -- where customers fund direct interconnection costs, while broader
system upgrades that benefit the grid are addressed in a way to not disadvantage early-moving
projects or communities.

Texas has built its reputation as the best place in the country to do business by working
collaboratively to solve challenges and enable growth. Texas has also demonstrated a willingness
to stand for national interests, particularly in micro-processing and biopharma manufacturing,
when facing global challenges. We must ensure this focus remains true as we look to the future.

Bryan stands ready to be part of the solution. We are committed to working with the Commission,
state leadership, and our partners across Texas to ensure we get this right—supporting reliability
while enabling the kind of economic development that drives long-term prosperity.

Thank you for your leadership and for your consideration of these comments.

Sincerely,




Bobby Gutierrez
Mayor, City of Bryan, Texas
